Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Work modulo \(397\). Since \(397\) is prime, we may invert nonzero residues.

First note that \(a_n+1\not\equiv 0\pmod{397}\) for any \(n\), because otherwise the congruence would give
\[
0\equiv a_n\equiv -1 \pmod{397},
\]
impossible. Thus
\[
a_{n+1}\equiv a_n(a_n+1)^{-2}\pmod{397}.
\]

Define an auxiliary sequence \(x_0,x_1,x_2,\ldots\) in \(\mathbb F_{397}\) by
\[
x_0=1,\qquad x_{n+1}=x_n+x_n^{-1}.
\]

We claim that
\[
a_n\equiv x_n^{-2}\pmod{397}
\]
for all \(n\). This is true for \(n=0\). If it is true for \(n\), then
\[
a_{n+1}
\equiv \frac{x_n^{-2}}{(x_n^{-2}+1)^2}
= \frac{x_n^2}{(x_n^2+1)^2}.
\]
But
\[
x_{n+1}=x_n+x_n^{-1}=\frac{x_n^2+1}{x_n},
\]
so
\[
x_{n+1}^{-2}=\frac{x_n^2}{(x_n^2+1)^2}.
\]
Hence \(a_{n+1}\equiv x_{n+1}^{-2}\), proving the claim.

Now square the recurrence for \(x_n\):
\[
x_{n+1}^2=(x_n+x_n^{-1})^2=x_n^2+2+x_n^{-2}.
\]
Since \(a_n\equiv x_n^{-2}\), we get
\[
a_n\equiv x_{n+1}^2-x_n^2-2.
\]

Therefore, for any \(N\),
\[
\sum_{n=0}^N a_n
\equiv \sum_{n=0}^N (x_{n+1}^2-x_n^2-2)
= x_{N+1}^2-x_0^2-2(N+1).
\]
Because \(x_0=1\),
\[
\sum_{n=0}^N a_n \equiv x_{N+1}^2-1-2(N+1).
\]

Also,
\[
x_{N+1}^2=x_N^2+2+x_N^{-2}=a_N^{-1}+2+a_N.
\]
Thus
\[
\sum_{n=0}^N a_n
\equiv a_N+a_N^{-1}-1-2N.
\]

Take \(N=2026\). We are given \(a_{2026}=9\). We need \(9^{-1}\pmod{397}\). Since
\[
397=9\cdot 44+1,
\]
we have
\[
9^{-1}\equiv -44\equiv 353\pmod{397}.
\]
Also,
\[
2(2026)+1=4053\equiv 83\pmod{397}.
\]
So
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv 9+353-83
\equiv 279\pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
